sourceBasis.bookAlignment: Question coverage is aligned with the prescribed-book themes relevant to the R-2025 Unit I scope. The questions are original ACADRIX study questions and do not reproduce textbook passages.

questions.q: What is Mechanical Engineering?
questions.a: The engineering discipline concerned with the design, analysis, manufacture, operation and maintenance of machines, devices and energy systems.

questions.q: What is the main role of a mechanical engineer?
questions.a: To apply engineering science and design methods to develop, analyse, manufacture, operate and improve mechanical systems.

questions.q: Name one early simple machine used in engineering.
questions.a: Lever.

questions.q: What major development accelerated mechanical engineering during the Industrial Revolution?
questions.a: Steam power and mechanised production, together with the development of machine tools.

questions.q: What is force?
questions.a: An interaction that can change the motion of a body or deform it.

questions.q: Is force a scalar or vector quantity?
questions.a: Vector quantity.

questions.q: What is the SI unit of force?
questions.a: Newton (N).

questions.q: Write the SI definition of one newton.
questions.a: 1 N = 1 kg·m/s².

questions.q: State Newton's second law in equation form.
questions.a: ΣF = ma.

questions.q: What is motion?
questions.a: The change of position of a body with time relative to a reference frame.

questions.q: Define displacement.
questions.a: The directed change in position of a body.

questions.q: Define velocity.
questions.a: The rate of change of displacement with time.

questions.q: Write the equation for velocity in terms of displacement.
questions.a: v = ds/dt.

questions.q: Define acceleration.
questions.a: The rate of change of velocity with time.

questions.q: Write the SI unit of acceleration.
questions.a: m/s².

questions.q: What is work?
questions.a: Work is done when a force causes displacement through the component of force in the displacement direction.

questions.q: Write the work equation for a constant force.
questions.a: W = Fs cosθ.

questions.q: What is the SI unit of work?
questions.a: Joule (J).

questions.q: When is the work done by a force zero?
questions.a: When the force is perpendicular to the displacement, for a constant force.

questions.q: Define energy.
questions.a: Energy is the capacity to do work.

questions.q: Write the expression for kinetic energy.
questions.a: KE = ½mv².

questions.q: Write the expression for gravitational potential energy near Earth's surface.
questions.a: PE = mgh.

questions.q: State the principle of conservation of energy for an ideal isolated mechanical system.
questions.a: Energy cannot be created or destroyed; it changes from one form to another while the total energy remains conserved.

questions.q: Define power.
questions.a: Power is the rate at which work is done or energy is transferred.

questions.q: Write the expression for power in terms of work and time.
questions.a: P = dW/dt; for average power, P = W/t.

questions.q: What is the SI unit of power?
questions.a: Watt (W).

questions.q: What is the relation between watt and joule per second?
What are dimensions?
questions.a: Dimensions describe how a physical quantity depends on fundamental physical quantities.

questions.q: What is dimensional analysis used for?
questions.a: It is used to check dimensional consistency of equations and assist in unit conversion and engineering estimation.

questions.q: Write the dimensions of force.
questions.a: MLT⁻².

questions.q: Write the dimensions of work or energy.
questions.a: ML²T⁻².

questions.q: Write the dimensions of power.
questions.a: ML²T⁻³.

questions.q: What is dimensional homogeneity?
questions.a: An equation is dimensionally homogeneous when all terms in the equation have the same dimensions.

questions.q: What does SI stand for?
questions.a: International System of Units.

questions.q: What is the SI base unit of length?
questions.a: Metre (m).

questions.q: What is the SI base unit of mass?
questions.a: Kilogram (kg).

questions.q: What is the SI base unit of time?
questions.a: Second (s).

questions.q: What is one important reason for using consistent units in engineering calculations?
questions.a: To ensure numerical calculations and equations are physically and dimensionally consistent.

questions.q: State one core responsibility of an engineer concerning public safety.
questions.a: To protect public safety and welfare in engineering decisions and practice.

questions.q: Why should an engineer work within their competence?
questions.a: To ensure technical decisions are made responsibly and safely, seeking appropriate expert support when necessary.

questions.q: What is a conflict of interest in professional engineering?
questions.a: A situation in which personal or external interests could improperly influence, or appear to influence, professional judgement.

questions.q: Why should engineers consider environmental impacts?
questions.a: Engineering decisions can affect resources, ecosystems and society, so responsible practice considers environmental consequences.

questions.q: Name two modern technologies that have transformed Mechanical Engineering.
questions.a: Examples include CAD/CAE, CNC, robotics, additive manufacturing and smart manufacturing.

questions.q: What is the SI unit of pressure?
questions.a: Pascal (Pa).

questions.q: Write the dimensions of pressure.
questions.a: ML⁻¹T⁻².
